title: "User's Guide"

---

The User's Guide covers conceptual background and practical tutorials for
bgms. It is organized into four parts: background concepts, model types,
analysis workflows, and MCMC output.

### Background

- [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd) — Installation and first model fit
- [Graphical Models](graphical-models.qmd) — Nodes, edges, and conditional independence
- [The Bayesian Approach](bayesian-approach.qmd) — Priors, posteriors, and Bayes factors
- [Prior Basics](prior-basics.qmd) — How `bgms` uses priors and when to change defaults

### Models

- [Gaussian Graphical Model](ggm.qmd) — Continuous data, partial associations, precision matrix
- [Ordinal MRF](omrf.qmd) — Binary and ordinal data, category thresholds, partial associations
- [Mixed MRF](mixed-model.qmd) — Datasets with both continuous and discrete variables

### Analyses

- [Edge Selection](edge-selection.qmd) — Spike-and-slab priors for structure learning
- [Group Comparison](group-comparison.qmd) — Comparing networks across groups with [`bgmCompare()`](../reference/bgmCompare.qmd)
- [Edge Clustering](clustering.qmd) — Stochastic block model prior for discovering edge clusters

### MCMC Output

- [MCMC Output](mcmc-output.qmd) — What the sampler returns and how to access it
- [MCMC Diagnostics](mcmc-diagnostics.qmd) — Convergence checks: ESS, R-hat, trace plots, divergences

### Prerequisites

This guide assumes basic familiarity with R programming and the goals of
network analysis. The [Background](#background) chapters introduce the
necessary statistical concepts.
